Subject: Re: Performance SLO & VPC network follow-up - Acme / next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our side so we can validate performance for the Private/VPC deployment: 

- Target SLOs you mentioned: 99th percentile latency target of 150ms for short text-generation requests, 95th percentile <= 50ms for embeddings endpoints used in search, and sustained throughput target of ~200 QPS for peak burst windows.
- Concurrency model: expect ~120 concurrent active sessions during peak, with ~20 of those using streaming (server->client) for progressive responses.
- Streaming requirements: low-latency chunk delivery (sub-100ms chunk spacing) and ability to early-flush partial tokens.
- Network constraints to validate: private peering preferred; otherwise, site-to-site VPN. We need to validate egress capacity, NAT/firewall timeouts, and whether you can peer via direct connect or cloud interconnect.

Next steps: 
1) I attached a preliminary SLO matrix and a network-path diagram for the private deployment. Please share any internal network contact who can provide topology and egress peering options.
2) If you can provide a simple network test (ping/traceroute from your VPC to our regional ingress IPs) and a perf sample (p95 of baseline requests) we can run an initial profile and advise kernel/quantization / batching knobs.
3) Jordan will follow up on procurement questions and DocuSign cadence.

Attachments: slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-path-diagram.pdf (diagram)

Thanks — available Tue/Wed afternoon for a short follow-up to review the network results.

—

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 150ms p99 target is for our UI synchronous calls (mostly short prompts), embeddings p95 <= 50ms is correct for search.
- Peak throughput: 200 QPS is accurate; sustained daily avg is around 40 QPS. Bursts typically last 1-3 minutes.
- Concurrency: 120 active sessions is reasonable; ~15-25 streaming sessions during peaks. We use streaming in our chat app for progressive delivery — sub-100ms chunk spacing is ideal.

Network details: 
- We prefer private peering via AWS Direct Connect in us-west-2. If that's not available we can use a site-to-site VPN (Transit Gateway) but will need NAT egress sizing.
- Our infra team needs the list of ingress IPs and port ranges to open (and whether we need to allow long-lived websockets or use keep-alive HTTP/2).

I'll loop in Priya (procurement) separately for the procurement/DocuSign timeline. Also looping in our network lead in the next email.

Alex — appreciate the details. A few more specifics from the engineering side that will help us validate quickly: 

- Ingress IPs / ports: we'll provide a small set of regional ingress IPs (4 addresses) and TCP 443 for HTTP/2 and websockets. We recommend enabling long-lived HTTP/2 with keep-alives for streaming flows; fallback to chunked HTTP/1.1 streaming is supported but incurs slightly higher latency.
- Protocol: streaming is over HTTP/2 server-push/streaming or websocket if you prefer. We typically recommend HTTP/2 for simpler NAT traversal and connection reuse.
- NAT/Firewall timeouts: please ensure idle timeouts > 5 minutes for long-lived sessions. We can send a short synthetic workload to detect premature timeouts.
- Egress sizing: for 200 QPS at ~1.2KB payloads and streaming overhead expect ~2-3 Gbps during peak bursts. Confirm available egress headroom.
- Kernel/tuning: we will run a profiling pass and may recommend TCP SACK/queue tuning and larger socket buffers; we can provide a short checklist for your infra team.

Attachments: redwood-qualification-checklist.docx (checklist)

Can your network lead run a traceroute to the attached regional ingress IPs (I added them in the Drive link) and share results? If you prefer, we can run an agent from your VPC as part of an onboarding lab — requires a simple IAM role.

I can jump on a 30-min call Tue 11am PT if that helps to go through the checklist with your network engineer.

Thanks —
Marissa
